one_line_reason: A single-ingredient RCT of pure theobromine supplementation in metabolic syndrome and an older exercise-performance review provide real (if modest) human efficacy evidence.

selected.population: overweight/obese adults aged 40-55 with metabolic syndrome (n=72 completers)
selected.intervention: pure theobromine 450 mg/day oral, both arms also following a low-calorie diet, 12 weeks vs placebo+diet
selected.primary_outcome: anthropometric and metabolic syndrome indices (waist circumference, lipid ratios, HDL-c)
selected.why_selected: The only shortlisted RCT of theobromine as a standalone oral supplement (both arms shared the same background diet), with a stated dose and modest but statistically significant favorable lipid/waist changes

selected.population: healthy subjects (single small theobromine study, 7-15 subjects)
selected.intervention: oral theobromine, single-dose or short-term (exact dose not given in this review-level abstract)
selected.primary_outcome: exercise performance (3 km treadmill time trial)
selected.why_selected: Older human data showing theobromine outperformed placebo and matched caffeine on a time trial, though it is a single very small study summarized within a broader review

blockers: 37615657 dosed theobromine on top of a shared low-calorie diet in both arms; effect sizes are small and diet is a major co-intervention even though it was matched between groups
33188564 is a narrative summary of a single small (7-15 subject) exercise study; the review itself does not restate the theobromine dose or full methodology

excluded_pmids.reason: In vitro dental-enamel remineralization study (topical, not human oral supplementation, and not human at all)

Epidemiological review of dietary methylxanthines (caffeine, theophylline, theobromine pooled together) and colorectal cancer; no theobromine-isolated human trial data, and the meta-analysis found no association for caffeine specifically
Observational review of whole chocolate consumption and preeclampsia risk in pregnant women; dietary whole-food exposure, not an isolated theobromine supplement, and a clinical/pregnant population
Reviews pentoxifylline, a synthetic theobromine-derivative drug, in preterm neonates; different (synthetic, prescription) compound, not the natural supplement ingredient
Urinary stone disease management guideline; no theobromine-specific content evident in the retrieved abstract
RCT of whole dark chocolate (flavonoids, polyphenols, magnesium, and theobromine together) on athletic performance; a multi-compound whole-food matrix, not an isolated theobromine exposure
RCT of caffeine ingestion in cyclists; theobromine and theophylline are measured only as endogenous metabolites of caffeine, not administered as the exposure
RCT of cocoa flavanol supplementation; the placebo was explicitly caffeine- and theobromine-matched, meaning theobromine was held constant/not the tested exposure
Cochrane review of cocoa/flavanol-rich chocolate on blood pressure; the studied active is flavanols, not theobromine, and exposure is whole cocoa product
Lipidomic/metabolomic analysis of a low-carbohydrate diet and HIIT; no theobromine exposure studied
